body: A ratio compares quantities by division. The ratio 2 to 3 is equal to 4 to 6 because both quantities increased by the same factor. If both quantities are lengths, convert them to the same unit before comparing them. A rate such as distance traveled per time compares different kinds of quantities and carries units.

A proportion states that two ratios are equal. If a drawing uses one length unit to represent five of the same unit on an object, a feature three units long in the drawing represents fifteen units. This calculation relies on the same scale factor being used for every length in the comparison.

limitations: A projection of a large curved surface onto a flat map can vary in scale. The scale of a lens image can also depend on the depth of the object.
purpose: Teach how ratios compare quantities and make diagrams readable at different scales.
